  "headline": "Intake established the browser game outcome, delivery boundaries, and discovery questions.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "summary": "S1 — Fact: deliver a small single-player Battleship game playable in a browser against a computer; the named browser is the authorized place for the outcome to become usable. Discovery must establish the available hosting environment and runtime capabilities before selecting an entry point or release method; this blocks a deployment plan, not initial design. Recorded defaults: one human and one computer opponent per game; a browser session identifies the human without an account; game state is not shared across people, devices, or sessions and lasts until the session ends or the player starts over; the computer's unhit ship locations stay hidden from the player. These defaults rule out multiplayer, cross-session continuity, and revealing the computer's fleet during play. Discovery must check whether the runtime already provides session or persistence features and establish the applicable Battleship rules before finalizing game behavior; absent evidence, use conventional rules and in-session state. Risks to check include exposing hidden fleet state and making the computer opponent unplayable. S2 — Fact: use Node.js for the server and include tests; discovery must establish the available Node.js version and existing test tooling before selecting dependencies and commands, with Node.js built-in testing as the recorded default if suitable. Run boundary: the repository is empty and this intake implements nothing; discovery has no named team, workspace, channel, internal site, document, private repository, owner, or ambiguous-term source hint in the request. No sensitive locator is supplied. Visibility: the isolated source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return; the game becomes visible in a deployed target only after release. A specific deployed target is not named, so its selection remains open to discovery and any person-only decision blocks that deployment only."
}
